commits_this_run: c16dd9b feat(ops-policy): expose policies-in-force list, count and source name (NEX-083)
decisions_this_run: An empty policy set is a 200 with an empty list, never a 404. Absence of policy is a valid answer; a 404 there would be indistinguishable from the operator gate refusing, and a caller could not tell 'no policies' from 'not allowed'.

The aggregate (policies, policy_count, source_name) is built in the application use case, not the router. The transport layer must not be where a contract shape is decided, or a second interface would have to re-derive it.

source_name reports which store answered rather than a boolean 'durable'. A caller that needs to know whether it is looking at the in-memory ring or the SQL adapter needs the name, and a boolean would lose the third adapter.

The non-operator 404 test was rebuilt on BOB. The previous DAVE-based version was 401 (DAVE is suspended, so the request failed authentication before reaching the gate) - the assertion passed, but for the wrong reason, and would not have caught a gate regression.
run_summary: Run 83 delivered NEX-083: the policy lifecycle could write (draft, publish, rollback, revoke) and could ask whether a policy was in force, but could not list what was in force. GET /api/v1/ops/policies/in-force now returns `policies`, `policy_count` and `source_name`, built in the use case and wired through the container and router. Empty set is 200, not 404, because 'no policies' and 'not allowed' must not look the same. Tests cover the empty set, a single published policy counting as one, and a genuine gate refusal. Local gates all green: ruff format/check clean, mypy clean across 143 files, full pytest suite exit 0, 66 targeted tests passed. CI was polled but both runs on c16dd9b were still in_progress at the budget boundary - NEX-083 is COMMITTED + PUSHED, not VERIFIED.
